name: Balikligol and the Old City
tagline: The sacred pools, the bazaar and the atmosphere
description: The historic core around the Pool of Abraham with its sacred carp, the Mevlid-i Halil mosque and the covered bazaar running north from it. It is the most atmospheric part of any Turkish city outside Istanbul, and the archaeological museum is a short walk away.
bestFor: Anyone here for the archaeology and the old city itself
pros: Balikligol, the bazaar and the museum all walkable
The most characterful accommodation in the city
cons: Very busy with domestic pilgrims and tourists
Brutally hot and shadeless in summer

name: Haliliye
tagline: The central district with the everyday services
description: The administrative and commercial district spreading north and east of the old city, holding the modern shops, the offices and much of the mid-range apartment stock. It is functional rather than beautiful and it is where most of the city's ordinary business is done.
bestFor: Longer stays needing services within reach of the old city
pros: Walking distance to the old city
Banks, shops and services all here
Better apartment stock than the historic centre
cons: Heavy traffic on the main arteries
Few places open in the evening

name: Karakopru
tagline: The newer northern district with the best housing
description: The modern residential district north of the centre, built out over the last two decades with newer apartment blocks, wider streets and the shopping centres. It has the best internet and the most comfortable housing in the city and none of the historic interest.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising a comfortable flat and a fast connection
pros: Newest apartments and best fibre coverage
Quieter and cleaner than the centre
cons: A taxi ride from the old city

name: Eyyubiye
tagline: The southern district, cheapest and most local
description: The large district south of the old city, dense, working class and home to much of the city's Syrian population. Rents are the lowest in Sanliurfa and daily life here happens entirely in Turkish and Arabic with no concession to outsiders at all.
bestFor: Very long stays on a minimal budget with the language to manage
pros: The lowest rents anywhere in the city
Close to the old city by road
cons: Services and infrastructure are weakest here
No English and little Turkish spoken slowly
Dense and hard going in summer heat
